pairs: And the Lord said to Moses:
For I have hardened his heart,
ut faciam signa mea hæc in eo:
so that I may accomplish these, my signs, in him,
et narres in auribus filii tui, et nepotum tuorum, quoties contriverim Ægyptios, et signa mea fecerim in eis: et sciatis quia ego Dominus.
and so that you may describe to the ears of your sons and your grandsons how often I opposed the Egyptians and wrought my signs among them, and so that you may know that I am the Lord.”
Introierunt ergo Moyses et Aaron ad Pharaonem,
Moses and Aaron entered to Pharaoh,
“Thus says the Lord God of the Hebrews:
How long will you be unwilling to be subject to me?
Release my people to sacrifice to me.
Sin autem resistis, et non vis dimittere eum:
But if you resist, and you are unwilling to release them,
ecce ego inducam cras locustam in fines tuos:
behold, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your borders.
And they shall cover the face of the earth,
lest any part of it be seen. Yes,
sed comedatur quod residuum fuerit grandini:
and what remains from the hail shall be eaten.
corrodet enim omnia ligna quæ germinant in agris.
For they will gnaw away all the trees that spring up in the fields.
And they will fill your houses,
ex quo orti sunt super terram,
from the time that they rose up over the earth,
Dixerunt autem servi Pharaonis ad eum:
Then the servants of Pharaoh said to him:
“How long must we endure this scandal?
in order to sacrifice to the Lord their God.
Do you not see that Egypt is perishing?”
Revocaveruntque Moysen et Aaron ad Pharaonem:
And they called back Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh,
sacrifice to the Lord your God.
Who are they who would go?”
Cum parvulis nostris, et senioribus pergemus,
“We will travel with our little ones and our elderly,
est enim solemnitas Domini Dei nostri.
For it is a solemnity of the Lord our God.”
“So let the Lord be with you.
But if I were to release you
cui dubium est quod pessime cogitetis?
who would doubt that you intend some great wickedness?
However, go only with the men,
and sacrifice to the Lord. For this,
too, is what you yourselves requested.”
Statimque ejecti sunt de conspectu Pharaonis.
And immediately they were cast out from the sight of Pharaoh.
Then the Lord said to Moses:
Extende manum tuam super terram Ægypti ad locustam,
“Extend your hand over the land of Egypt, toward the locusts,
ut ascendat super eam, et devoret omnem herbam quæ residua fuerit grandini.
so that they may rise up over it, and devour every plant which remains from the hail.”
Et extendit Moyses virgam super terram Ægypti:
And Moses extended his staff over the land of Egypt.
et Dominus induxit ventum urentem tota die illa et nocte:
And the Lord brought a burning wind all that day and night.
the burning wind lifted up the locusts.
Quæ ascenderunt super universam terram Ægypti:
And they ascended over the entire land of Egypt.
et sederunt in cunctis finibus Ægyptiorum innumerabiles,
And they settled into all the parts of the Egyptians: innumerable,
quales ante illud tempus non fuerant,
such as had not been before that time,
And they covered the entire face of the land,
And the plants of the land were devoured,
et quidquid pomorum in arboribus fuit,
along with whatever fruits were on the trees,
which the hail had left behind.
nihilque omnino virens relictum est in lignis et in herbis terræ,
And nothing at all of the greenery remained on the trees
or on the plants of the earth in all of Egypt.
Quam ob rem festinus Pharao vocavit Moysen
Pharaoh hurriedly called Moses and Aaron,
“I have sinned against the Lord your God,
Sed nunc dimittite peccatum mihi etiam hac vice,
But now, release me from my sin even this time,
and petition the Lord your God,
ut auferat a me mortem istam.
so that he may take this death away from me.”
And Moses, departing from the sight of Pharaoh,
Qui flare fecit ventum ab occidente vehementissimum,
And he caused a very strong wind to blow from the west, and,
et arreptam locustam projecit in mare Rubrum:
seizing the locusts, it cast them into the Red Sea.
non remansit ne una quidem in cunctis finibus Ægypti.
There remained not so much as one in all the parts of Egypt.
And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh;
neither did he release the sons of Israel.
Then the Lord said to Moses:
et sint tenebræ super terram Ægypti tam densæ,
And let there be a darkness over the land of Egypt,
so dense that they may be able to feel it.”
And Moses extended his hand into the sky.
et factæ sunt tenebræ horribiles in universa terra Ægypti tribus diebus.
And there came a horrible darkness in the entire land of Egypt for three days.
nec movit se de loco in quo erat:
nor moved himself out of the place where he was.
But wherever the sons of Israel were living,
And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron,
oves tantum vestræ et armenta remaneant,
Only let your sheep and herds remain behind.
Your little ones may go with you.”
Hostias quoque et holocausta dabis nobis,
“You must also permit us victims and holocausts,
which we may offer to the Lord our God.
All the flocks shall travel with us.
Not one hoof of them shall remain behind.
quæ necessaria sunt in cultum Domini Dei nostri:
For they are necessary for the worship of the Lord our God,
præsertim cum ignoremus quid debeat immolari,
especially since we do not know what ought to be immolated,
until we arrive at the very place.”
But the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh,
and he was not willing to release them.
et cave ne ultra videas faciem meam:
and beware that you no longer see my face.
On whatever day you will appear in my sight,
“So be it, just as you have said.
I will no longer see your face.”
